architecture: EfficientNetB0 (ImageNet weights, frozen) wrapped in TimeDistributed, two GRU layers (256 then 128), Dense(1024) + softmax(10)

input.frame_selection: uniform over the detected action window when available, otherwise uniform over the clip
input.resize: bilinear resize preserving aspect ratio, centred zero padding
input.note: The graph starts with Rescaling(1/255) and ImageNet normalisation, so 0-255 input is required. The upstream Streamlit demo fed 0-1 frames, which is a preprocessing bug in that demo.

note: Experimental shot hint. The model was trained on broadcast cricket footage and is unreliable on phone-recorded practice clips. Read the measured benchmark before trusting any label.
limitations: Trained on broadcast footage: tight framing, match context, and a fixed camera.
On this project's 44 labelled phone clips it reached 34% top-1 and 57% top-2, and predicted straight_drive for most clips.
Confidence is not calibrated: mean confidence was higher for wrong predictions than for right ones.
Unsupported shots such as reverse sweep and scoop are forced into one of the ten classes.
Not a substitute for a coach's judgement.

benchmark.dataset: This project's historical phone clips (single athlete, two recording sessions)
benchmark.interpretation: Broadcast-trained weights do not transfer to indoor phone clips. The model is deployed only as an explicitly experimental hint; it is not used for coaching claims.

provenance.weights_license: Published under the source repository's MIT license
provenance.training_data: Announced as sourced from CricShotClassify (Sen et al., Sensors 2021); dataset redistribution and commercial-use terms are unverified
provenance.conversion: Keras HDF5 to ONNX, validated against a reconstructed TensorFlow graph (max absolute output difference 1.06e-9). Unused initializer removed; outputs verified bit-identical.
provenance.commercial_use: Not cleared. Treat as a research/demo baseline until the dataset terms are reviewed.
